title: A 1 nS relay-edge cap requires a direct share of at least 31 percent in 31 Allen-based admittance models
abstract: We tested a conductance limit left open by prior hidden-relay models. A Schur-complement bound gives the minimum direct share of effective DC mutual conductance when one passive hidden node has capacitance at least 1 pF and each relay edge is at most 1 nS. If cross-admittance stays within 5 percent of an ideal direct-edge response through 100 Hz, the minimum direct share is 31.76 to 77.08 percent in 31 Allen mouse cortex reference models. Explicit positive-leak circuits attain every limit while preserving the full reference DC matrix. Peak-resistance references give 32.03 to 75.24 percent. Independent full-matrix checks pass for 62 circuits. The frequency response and parameter limits are assumed, not measured. Multiple hidden nodes and active elements are outside the result. Original code, aggregate results, a proof, source hashes and external regeneration steps are supplied.

display.caption: Necessary relay-only exclusions as the edge cap changes, and sharp minimum direct shares at a 1 nS cap. These are conditional model results, not measured junction shares.
